observations: Photo 0 shows a used internal combustion engine sitting on dirt ground.
The engine has a V-configuration intake manifold with two cylinder banks visible.
The valve cover has embossed lettering, but it is not legible in this photo.
The background is stacked with used engine parts such as cylinder heads.
No gearbox or transmission is clearly visible attached to or beside the engine.
No readable brand badge, model plate, VIN, engine code, or year marking is visible in the photo.

claims.claim: Honda accord 2004 engine and gear box ka24
claims.evidence: No readable Honda, Accord, 2004, or ka24 marking is visible in photo 0; ka24 is a Nissan engine code, not Honda, but this cannot be confirmed from the photos alone.

risks.risk: The engine may be seized, damaged, or internally worn and not runnable.
risks.proof: A video of the engine turning over by hand or running, plus a compression test result.

risks.risk: The claimed gearbox may be missing, mismatched, or damaged.
risks.proof: A clear photo showing the gearbox/transmission included with the engine.

risks.risk: The engine may not be a Honda Accord 2004 ka24 as claimed.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the engine block stamp or valve cover with readable brand, model, and engine code.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of any readable stamp, plate, or casting on the engine block and valve cover.
Photo showing the gearbox/transmission if it is included.
Video of the engine turning over or running.
response.reason: The item is visibly a used car engine, but no brand, model, year, or engine code can be read from the photo, and the seller's claim mixes a Honda car with a Nissan engine code; it is priced at its worst case as a non-working, unidentified engine until proof is provided.
